clue.text: Under a captain's vessel, vary nitrogen

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a vessel
to vary is to alter
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Someone on board a ship takes nitrogen readings under the captain's orders.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the definition as 'Under a captain is': a subaltern is an army officer below the rank of captain, so 'vessel' is not the captain's ship at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A subaltern is a junior army officer, ranking below a captain.

clue.text: Part of flight with Brummie in lead

indicators.note: in places the setter's pronoun inside the word for the lead

parts.note: the lead in a film or show is its star
Brummie is the setter's pseudonym, so the setter is I

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be in the lead on part of a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Brummie is the setter, so the name gives I, the setter speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is made of individual steps, each one a stair.

clue.text: Even less able to view outstanding performance

definitions.meaning: comparative of blind: having still less sight
a dazzling, superb display in sport, British slang

explanation.definitionFit: Blind means unable to see, so the comparative is less able still; separately, British slang calls a brilliant performance a blinder.

clue.text: Push end of toboggan into toboggan

indicators.note: into places the final letter inside the small sled word

parts.note: a luge is a small toboggan raced lying on the back

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the first toboggan

explanation.surface: Someone gives a toboggan a shove, oddly described as putting its end into itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of toboggan' gives N, which goes inside LUGE, the second 'toboggan'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust, a push.

clue.text: Days before theatrical Midlands town

parts.note: an eve is the day before an event, so days before are eves
a ham is an over-theatrical actor; ham also means overacted

explanation.surface: A period of days ahead of some theatrical event in the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: EVESHAM is a market town in Worcestershire, in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Evesham is a real market town in Worcestershire, in central England.

clue.text: Meetings here offering up-to-the-minute commercial opportunity

parts.note: something up-to-the-minute is new
a market is an opening for selling goods

explanation.surface: A business pitch for a fresh opening where people can trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meetings' are race meetings: NEWMARKET in Suffolk is the headquarters of British horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket racecourse in Suffolk holds horse-race meetings, so race meetings take place there.

clue.text: Break horny musician's back

indicators.note: back tells us the possessive name is read from its end

parts.note: Pan, the horned Greek god, played the pipes; Pan's gives PANS

explanation.surface: Something breaks the back of a randy musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horny' suggests lust, but it means horned: the goat-legged god Pan, with his pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap is to break suddenly and cleanly.

clue.text: Mollusc in eg summer? Not on tug

indicators.note: Not tells us the following small word is left out of the time of year

parts.note: summer is an example of a season
taken as written
to lug is to tug or haul

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about something spotted in summer, with a tug boat mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' drops the small word on from the end of the season, so 'in eg summer' is not a location at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea slug is a shell-less marine gastropod, a kind of mollusc.

clue.text: Racing ace forced out — angry

parts.note: A is short for ace in cards

indicators.note: forced suggests the word out is pushed into a new order

parts.note: cross means angry

explanation.surface: A top driver is forced out of a race and furious about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' gives UTO; 'Racing' looks like an adjective for the ace, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Autocross is a form of motor racing on grass or dirt courses.

clue.text: People treated broadcast as a theatrical work

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is spoken over the air, so we go by its sound

parts.note: people under medical treatment are patients

explanation.surface: Hospital cases are presented on the radio as a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote a comic opera of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, a stage work.

clue.text: Radium-enriched, inclusive of spirit

indicators.note: enriched means the word gains the element's symbol inside it

parts.note: inclusive of means with
Ra is the chemical symbol for radium

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about something enriched with radium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enriched' signals the insertion: the element is added inside, as a metal is enriched by an additive.
explanation.definitionFit: A wraith is a ghost, an apparition or spirit.

clue.text: Link broadcast just started before watershed

indicators.note: before puts the opening letter ahead of the hill line
just started means only the opening letter of broadcast is used

parts.note: a watershed is a ridge dividing two river systems

explanation.surface: A programme link screened just before the 9pm watershed on British TV.
explanation.walkthrough: The watershed is also the 9pm cut-off for adult TV in Britain, but here it is a dividing ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge links two banks, so it is a link or connection.

clue.text: Hold molten lead in wine

indicators.note: in puts the reworked metal inside the wine

parts.note: hock is German white wine

indicators.note: molten lead is melted and reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A metalworker pours molten lead into wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'molten' gives EADL; 'Hold' looks like a verb, but it is a wrestling noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlock is a wrestling grip around the head, a hold.

clue.text: Elf, back to front, showing liveliness

indicators.note: back to front means the final letter is taken to the start

parts.note: a sprite is an elf or fairy

explanation.surface: A mischievous elf turned round shows great vivacity.
explanation.walkthrough: The last E of SPRITE moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is lively wit and spirit, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Natural harbour demands sun hat on a swimming fowl

parts.note: a cap is a hat

indicators.note: swimming suggests the bird's letters drift into a new order

explanation.surface: A harbour requires a bird swimming there to wear a sun hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' turns FOWL into FLOW. SCAPA FLOW is a great natural anchorage in Orkney, off northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Scapa Flow is an enclosed body of water in Orkney used as a naval anchorage.

clue.text: Retired at end of day in mood for a significant age

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the word for mood

parts.note: tone is mood or atmosphere
to retire is to go to bed, so retired is went

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of day

explanation.surface: Someone goes to bed at the end of the day in a mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the pieces inside the mood word, splitting it after its first letter; twenty-one was the traditional British coming-of-age.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-one was the traditional age of coming of age, a milestone birthday.

clue.text: Prepare "sticky mess date" to give compensation

parts.note: to prepare a meal is to make it
goo is sticky mess

explanation.surface: Cooking up a gooey date dish as a peace offering.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good is to repair or compensate for a loss.

clue.text: Leader getting to sleep over, initially, with Trotsky?

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of over is used

parts.note: Leon Trotsky was the Russian revolutionary

explanation.surface: A leader drops off over a Trotsky biography.
explanation.walkthrough: In Orwell's Animal Farm the pig Napoleon is the leader and his rival Snowball is the Trotsky figure, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte led France; the name also suits the pig who leads in Animal Farm.

clue.text: Over-fussy type getting on potty holds one

parts.note: someone getting on in years is old

indicators.note: holds means the crazy word encloses the numeral

parts.note: potty is British slang for mad
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fussy person getting on, clutching a potty.
explanation.definitionFit: Old maid is a dated term for a prim, fussy person.

clue.text: Only dining chairs worthy of comment?

definitions.meaning: only chairs and no dining table: read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Notable means remarkable, worth noting; split in two it says there is no table.

clue.text: Philosophy of communist doctrine switching left and right wings

indicators.note: the wings are the outside letters, which change places

parts.note: Maoist describes the doctrine of Mao Zedong

explanation.surface: A philosophy grows out of communist doctrine as its factions trade places.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the M and T at the two ends of MAOIST: the wings are the outermost letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Taoism is the Chinese philosophy and religion founded on the teachings of Laozi.

clue.text: Show off more old hat, black, worn material

parts.note: something old hat is out of fashion, out
B is short for black, as on pencils
a rag is a piece of worn cloth

explanation.surface: An old hat in black, made of worn cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To outbrag is to boast more than another, outdoing them in showing off.

clue.text: Difficult answer — bird toiling

parts.note: hard means difficult
a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: A hard puzzle answer about a bird at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard at it is an idiom for working busily, so toiling.

clue.text: Attempt to remove government lay school

parts.note: to lay something down is to put it

explanation.surface: A move to topple the government is laid out by a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is a sudden attempt to overthrow a government, a coup.

clue.text: Authorisation put in for each rude attention-seeker?

indicators.note: put in says the approval goes inside the word for each

parts.note: per means for each
OK is approval or authorisation

explanation.surface: Permission is granted for every rude person seeking attention.
explanation.walkthrough: A poker is literally one who pokes, a rude way of getting someone's attention; hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pokes another to be noticed is jokingly a poker.

clue.text: TNT found in "Cat and Fiddle"

indicators.note: found in puts the explosive inside the animal

parts.note: taken as written
TNT is a high explosive, HE

explanation.surface: Explosives discovered at the Cat and Fiddle, a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for high explosive. The quoted pub name hides the definition at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle is to cheat, as in fiddling accounts.

clue.text: Boundary-less "help-a-son" city

indicators.note: boundary-less removes the outer letters of the quoted phrase

explanation.surface: A plea to help a son from a city without limits.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first and last letters H and N.
explanation.definitionFit: El Paso is a city in Texas on the Mexican border.

clue.text: Rolls producers using kinetic energy, initially located in Serbia, maybe

indicators.note: located in places the initials inside the rearranged country name
maybe suggests Serbia is only one possible arrangement of its letters
initially takes the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Bread producers in Serbia use kinetic energy for their ovens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' gives BARIES, and 'located in' sets the initials inside; 'Rolls' looks like the car maker, but it means bread rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakeries produce bread rolls among other baked goods.

clue.text: Heartlessly admitted hadn't repaid debt

indicators.note: heartlessly removes the central letter of the word

parts.note: to own up is to admit, so admitted is owned

explanation.surface: Someone coldly admitted they had not paid back a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Owed money is money one still has to pay, a debt not yet settled.

clue.text: So, no problem regarding military command?

definitions.text: So, no problem regarding military command?

parts.words: So, no problem regarding military command?
parts.note: a parade order to turn the head, read as a remark that one's sight is fine

explanation.definitionFit: Eyes right is a drill command to turn the head; read as a remark, it says the eyesight is fine.
